assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a unifying physical principle behind respiration, photosynthesis and water oxidation, and also underlies molecular electrocatalysis for fuels. The concept (concerted versus stepwise transfer, a quantum treatment of the proton) is original, clearly articulated and has changed how mechanisms in bioenergetics and catalysis are described. It sits close to my own field of proton transfer in respiratory enzymes, so I judge its centrality with some familiarity.
assessment.attribution: Mayer established bond-strength thermochemistry and the concerted PCET framework; Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theory that made the proton-electron couplings quantitative; Nocera contributed the PCET view of water oxidation and artificial photosynthesis. T. J. Meyer's early work is foundational, but a three-person prize needs a choice. The split between experiment and theory is workable but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, widely adopted terminology and teaching, and integration into enzyme mechanism studies. Recognition would be timely, not premature.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs foundational contributions by T. J. Meyer against later conceptual consolidation.
Some enzymatic PCET claims remain debated in detail.
Whether the topic reads as a coherent single discovery or a broad field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with small molecules to degrade chosen proteins is a new pharmacological modality with real chemical content: heterobifunctional design and the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide analogues. Impact is large and growing, with many compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explained molecular glues. Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure work made the approach drug-like. Credit is split across PROTAC concept, cereblon biology and VHL chemistry, and the eight-plus names make a clean three-person selection hard.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent validation across labs and clinical-stage compounds, but the first approved PROTAC drug is not yet established, so some of the clinical case is still maturing.
uncertainties: Which of the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages should be the core of the prize.
Clinical outcomes are still accumulating.
Medicine-oriented impact could shift the prize toward another prize body.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced one of the fastest rises in photovoltaic efficiency, with a new materials class and defect tolerance that challenged expectations. The importance for energy conversion is clear and the originality of the first sensitiser report and the solid-state devices is well documented.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell; Park and Snaith (with Grätzel and Seok) made the solid-state, efficient devices. The credit chain is contested and broad, with Grätzel and Kanatzidis also listed, which makes a trio difficult.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are confirmed across many groups, but long-term stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, which raises doubt about whether recognition is yet timely for an energy-conversion technology.
uncertainties: Operational stability remains unproven at scale.
Disputed priority between the sensitised and solid-state steps.
Unclear whether committee will favour materials with commercial maturity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins gave quantitative tests of Marcus theory in biological media, showing how distance, driving force and the intervening medium set tunnelling rates. It is conceptually fundamental for respiration and photosynthesis and is directly relevant to my own work on electron transfer in oxidases.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler were the decisive pair, using ruthenium-modified proteins and flash-quench methods. Credit is clean, although Marcus's prize (1992) and others' work (Dutton, Closs) overlap the topic.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed, with a long record, and now arguably late rather than premature. The risk is that it is seen as already implicitly recognised.
uncertainties: Possible perception that Marcus's prize covered the core insight.
Relative role of the pathways model versus the empirical tunnelling-timetable picture.
Whether Dutton's contributions should be acknowledged, but his name is not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyses N2 reduction at a unique Fe-Mo-S-C cofactor. The structures (including the central carbide) and the kinetic mechanism define a central problem in bioinorganic chemistry and in biological energy conversion. The scientific and societal significance is large.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle supplied structures of the MoFe protein and the cofactor; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism and genetics; Ribbe contributed cofactor biosynthesis and the cryo-EM state work. Credit is spread over structure and mechanism, so a trio is plausible but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the mechanism of N2 binding and the identity of the key intermediates are still being refined, so full maturity is incomplete.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism is still debated.
Distribution of credit between structure and mechanism groups.
Past prizes on Haber-Bosch and nitrogen fixation chemistry may count against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates formed by phase separation have reshaped the picture of cellular organisation and brought polymer physical chemistry into cell biology. The conceptual impact is large and generated broad research interest.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the key liquid-droplet observations (P granules); Rosen showed multivalent-interaction phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed the physical framework. Credit is plausible for three, with some contention over the theory side.
assessment.maturity: Younger and still contested as to physiological relevance; claims that many condensates are functional phase-separated liquids need caution, so I regard this as probably premature.
uncertainties: How many reported condensates are true liquid-liquid phase separation in vivo.
Whether the discovery is chemistry or cell biology.
Disputed role of theoretical contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single bases without double-strand breaks and was designed from first principles of nucleotide chemistry with evolved deaminases. It is original and highly consequential for genome engineering and therapeutics; its link to B061 (prime editing) means Liu's work as a whole may be recognised together.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the lead; Komor and Gaudelli were the first authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. A single laureate or Liu with the two trainees is the plausible configuration, and I treat the trainees' roles as secondary.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many groups with clinical trials under way. It follows CRISPR (2020) closely, which could make the committee hesitant about a near-duplicate genome-editing prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too close to the 2020 prize.
Fair credit for early-career coauthors.
Possible need to combine with prime editing in the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with reversible terminators and clustered arrays transformed biology and medicine. It is a real chemical invention with huge practical impact, and the underlying fluorescent nucleotide chemistry is clean.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the clearest originators of the Solexa chemistry; other credited names (Rothberg, Ju, Mayer) represent competing platforms, so I keep to two for a clean attribution.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature, widely validated and has had decades of impact. Timeliness is good, but the dispute among platforms and the Sanger-related prior prize make it less compelling than others.
uncertainties: Priority conflicts between sequencing platforms.
Whether it is seen as a technology rather than a discovery.
Commercial litigation history may complicate the narrative.
